facts.value: Table 3: Human evaluation with automatic-metric summary.
facts.where: Table 3 caption
facts.quote: Table 3: Human evaluation with automatic-metric summary. Per-dimension human scores are native-speaker judgments (weighted mean over 72 rows, 24 per language): Nat.=Naturalness/Fluency, Gram.=Grammar, Word=Word Choice, Reg.=Register, Usab.=Usability; Total is their sum (max 12). BGE-M3 and BERT-F1 are failure-aware means over all 142 responses per model. Eng.-only fails: genuine cases (excluding English-task prompts) where the model returned English instead of the romanized target.
facts.note: human scores = native-speaker judgments, weighted mean over 72 rows (24 per language); Total = sum (max 12); BGE-M3 and BERT-F1 = failure-aware means over all 142 responses per model

facts.quote: Table 4: Mean output tokens per model and language. Qwen Kannada excludes 49 degenerate rows; including them raises the Kannada mean to 1,768. Claude reports the highest stable token usage (1,068 average), followed by GPT-5.5 (714) and Gemini (678).
